title: World Clock Map: City Times Side by Side
description: See local clock times for picked cities side by side on the World Clock Map — coordination at a glance, DST applied live. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, one glance at four clocks — New York 9:00, London 14:00, Mumbai 19:30, Sydney already tomorrow — teaches more about a team's geography than a month of scheduling pain.
quick_answer: The World Clock Map shows the local times of cities you pick, side by side, for coordination at a glance. Add your cities and compare their clocks as they tick — with daylight-saving rules applied live, because a world clock that ignores changeover weeks is a poster, not a tool.
steps_intro: Every team's wall of clocks, without the wall:

body.t: Before proposing any time, look at everyone's now — the
turns the glance into a slot.
Call when both clocks say a kind hour. Grandparents' morning and grandchildren's evening find each other on this wall.
Opens, closes and kick-offs across exchanges and stadiums — the cities tick in their own business hours.
Nothing teaches zones like watching Tokyo eat lunch tomorrow while New York finishes yesterday's dinner. Live clocks beat diagrams.
Sydney regularly shows tomorrow's date while New York shows today — the date line made mundane, ticking on the same wall.
Mumbai's :30 offset ticks visibly against the hour-aligned cities — a small permanent lesson in why the world's clocks are not a grid.

popular_table.title: One instant, the wall's way
popular_table.intro: A winter moment, 14:00 UTC rendered on the classic cities — the map computes yours live.
popular_table.note: DST seasons shift rows by an hour here and there; the live map never uses this table's frozen rules — it computes from the tz database continuously.

faq: Yes — the displayed times update as time passes, computed from each city's zone rules rather than from a static offset table.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — cities are added by you; your own location joins the wall only if you add it.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
City resolutions come from open geocoding; the zone rules are the IANA database's, matching your devices' sources.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — it is never requested for the wall.
A wall's worth — the glance works for a handful to a dozen. Beyond that, the Meeting Time Planner's slot logic serves better than clocks.
Ticking displays follow the page's design; for timestamp-precision work the converter family gives exact instants.
A city is missing from the list.
Add by the nearest major city in the same zone, or resolve the exact point's zone with the Timezone Map Finder.
The wall's style is the page's; the arithmetic beneath — tz rules, live — is identical either way.
The wall applies rules live, so changeover weekends shift cities in front of you — the honest behaviour static posters cannot offer.
